summary: Hold: this hypothesis's own build condition has failed. Stage 1's 2-CTA slab multicast cut issued L2 bytes by 24-39% yet rega ran 1.31-1.38x slower at high/ft and 1.80x at low (OFF in every class, job 0ca60bb781db48e4), and the in-CTA bm256 byte cut also lost 1.16-1.21x (job a6f6063051f14750), so slab ingest is not the limiter and CL=4 widens exactly the cluster handshake that cost CL=2 ~0.3-0.5 us per stage. Spend the check on diagnosing that cost (or master's real limiter), not on CL=4.
justification: Its build condition (an issued-TB/s drop that moved time) failed in stage 1 (job 0ca60bb781db48e4): issued bytes fell 24-39% while rega_mc_kernel got 1.32-1.90x slower; bm256 (job a6f6063051f14750) cut the same ~38% bytes and also lost 1.16-1.20x. The ingest-cap premise behind DIAGNOSIS actions 1-2 is falsified; CL=4 widens the per-stage cluster handshake (4-way lockstep, 32-arrival empty barriers, 3 remote arrives per consumer warp per stage). Spec defects noted: tail-bucket boxes vs expect_tx, rank skipping at bucket 64, quad pairing in the decode.
confounders: experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096 / experts-turn-rega-s4-first-turn-n128: the incumbent's serial consumer, not ingest, sets the pace
align-two-phase-all-t-rega: fixes chunking k and the tail-bucket mix
combo-a-master-normgather-naive-stack: the gate must time the norm-gather-on routed block
interference: No companion warranted; the prepare gate already A/Bs master vs CL=2 vs CL=4. The open question is upstream: why CL=2 added ~0.3-0.5 us per stage.
open_questions: Re-scope: print-only variants (a) master rega as (2,1,1) clusters, (b) plus 16-arrival cross-CTA empty barrier, (c) stage-1 mc2, (d) mc2 with remote arrives spread across lanes at .release.cta
Re-diagnose master's limiter (clock64 stamps of the consumer's waits / dq_stage / wgmma_wait) before minting new rega stages
Siblings experts-rega-mc2-bm256-stack-high-ft and experts-rega-low-2cta-fullslab-mc2 share the falsified premise
The -cf confirm (13cfaf1e25c341af) re-measures master: its parent's gate kept master in high and ft
